strengths: Addresses important gap with first multiview object-level change detection benchmark with 350 diverse video pairs and comprehensive evaluation metrics (per-view, per-scene, per-scene AP_poly)

Comprehensive experimental evaluation including detailed ablation studies, systematic failure case analysis (geometry reconstruction, lighting changes, cluttered scenes), and robustness evaluations under varying conditions
Well-designed evaluation protocol with clear per-view tolerance policies and multi-level assessment suitable for different use cases
Training-free method leveraging existing pretrained models (π³, SAM, DINO3) shows pragmatic approach with reasonable generalization potential
Demonstrates practical applicability through robot manipulation use case (cleaning robot) beyond academic benchmarking
Clear presentation with informative visualizations, extensive supplementary materials, and detailed implementation specifications
weaknesses: Method component lacks algorithmic novelty - combines existing techniques (depth reconstruction, feature extraction, region scoring) in straightforward manner without innovative technical contributions
Significant computational efficiency problem: 159.4s per sequence pair vs VLM (30.5s) and CYWS-3D (23.9s) due to SAM mask generation bottleneck; 5-7x slowdown severely limits practical deployment
Persistent performance gaps with high sensitivity to multiple hyperparameters; absolute scores (e.g., 28.9 AP_poly on SD-V) indicate substantial unresolved challenges despite relative improvements

Dataset scale and scope limitations: only 350 video pairs, restricted to indoor environments, limited to small objects, and excludes dynamic objects; reliance on geometry reconstruction limits applicability to sparse/textureless scenes
Heavy dependence on pretrained models (π³, SAM, DINO3) introduces model-specific biases; explicitly acknowledged sensitivity to reconstruction failures prevents reliable deployment

Technical concerns including ad-hoc asymmetric depth handling, per-view evaluation allowing 2 FPs per ground-truth object may be overly lenient, empirically-tuned region merging strategy; reproducibility depends on multiple external dependencies not fully integrated

strengths: Novel and comprehensive multiview object change detection benchmark with 350 video pairs from 60 diverse scenes and 1,009 densely annotated objects, filling an important gap in existing benchmarks

Thorough experimental validation including ablation studies demonstrating component impact, hyperparameter sensitivity analysis, and evaluation across four existing datasets beyond the proposed benchmark
Well-motivated technical approach combining geometry reconstruction and semantic features with clear explanation of how 3D alignment disambiguates viewpoint/lighting changes from true scene changes
Strong empirical results showing 53% and 30.8% relative AP improvements over prior work on different benchmarks
Practical demonstration of real-world utility through robot cleaning application showing the method's applicability beyond academic metrics
Comprehensive annotation pipeline with semi-automatic tools and detailed protocols supporting reproducibility and future extensions
Commitment to reproducibility through promised release of dataset, annotation tool, code, and extensive supplementary material with implementation details
Clear presentation with informative visualizations effectively communicating dataset diversity and method pipeline
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty of the method—primarily orchestrates existing techniques (π³, SAM, DINO) with straightforward region matching rather than introducing novel algorithms
Training-free design sacrifices end-to-end optimization for generalization, limiting algorithmic contributions and relegating the method to pipeline design

Incomplete treatment of fundamental challenges: geometric reconstruction failures with limited overlap/textureless surfaces and strong lighting variations remain unresolved without novel mitigation strategies
Missing annotation quality metrics such as inter-annotator agreement, which would strengthen confidence in benchmark reliability given acknowledged ambiguity in change definitions
Dataset scale (350 videos from 60 scenes) is modest compared to major vision benchmarks, with most examples concentrated on tabletop/controlled indoor scenarios
Limited baseline comparisons with some using published results rather than re-implementations, and VLM evaluation restricted to a single model
Method assumptions (aligned scene geometry, similar camera trajectories) are implicit but not explicitly stated in limitations section
Computational efficiency not thoroughly analyzed despite sequential dependency on multiple large pretrained models, which could be a practical bottleneck
Generalization beyond tabletop/indoor manipulated scenarios to dynamic outdoor or highly cluttered real-world environments not thoroughly explored
